newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Out-of-the-money puts bought in Cadbury.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Out-of-the-money puts bought in Cadbury.

text.p: The UK stock options market was actively traded on Thursday as underlying shares roared ahead, dealers said.
But most deals were for relatively small lot sizes and dealers attributed this to market uncertainity about the current level of share prices.
"People want to take a position (in options) but with the market now at a record high, there is a feeling of just how much higher we can go from here," said one dealer.
The largest trade by early afternoon was from a buyer of 2,330 May 460 puts at 3p in Cadbury Schweppes.

Buying out-of-the-money puts offers a high reward in percentage terms if the underlying stock falls substantially but the deal may have been a hedge to protect against losses from holding shares in Cadbury.
By 1340 GMT, shares in the confectionery and soft drinks group gained 12-1/2p to 543-1/2p after positive analyst comment following the company's annual results on Wednesday.
Buying puts was also the main deal in Barclays Bank where 325 May 1000 puts were bought at 12p.
The bank's shares gained a penny to 1109-1/2p.

In diversified industrials group Tomkins there was a seller of 500 March 280 calls at 8-1/2p which may have been a closing deal or an attempt to capture time value premium before the options expire on March 19.
Over in FTSE 100 index options, the main deals were volatility trades in which traders are not so much concerned with market direction, but more with a change in its volatility.
The FTSE 100 index was up 34.5 at 4394.6 by 1340 GMT.
